body:
**Steps to Reproduce:**
- Install the Sale Project module.
- Navigate to the Project module.
- Enable Project Stages.
- Go to the Project list view.
- Observe that the Next Milestone does not display the deadline along with the milestone name.

**Issue:**
The milestone display name is incomplete and does not include the deadline date.

**Cause:**
The context overridden in sale project did not pass the required context, cause the display_name computation did not add deadline to the display name.

**Fix:**
Passed the appropriate context in the action context to ensure the display name is correctly computed and displayed with its deadline.

## 問題

PR #43でgithub-advanced-securityから以下の警告が報告されました：

> ## Workflow does not contain permissions
> 
> Actions job or workflow does not limit the permissions of the GITHUB_TOKEN. Consider setting an explicit permissions block, using the following as a minimal starting point: {}
> 
> [Show more details](https://github.com/Kazuki-0731/Kimigayo/security/code-scanning/28)

## 修正内容

`notify`ジョブに明示的な`permissions: {}`ブロックを追加し、GITHUB_TOKENの権限を最小限に制限しました。

### 変更箇所

#### `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
```yaml
  notify:
    name: Discord Notification
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [shellcheck, build-and-test, security-scan]
    if: always()
    permissions: {}  # 追加
    steps:
```

#### `.github/workflows/release.yml`
```yaml
  notify:
    name: Discord Notification
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [build-and-push, create-manifest, create-github-release]
    if: always()
    permissions: {}  # 追加
    steps:
```

## セキュリティ向上

`permissions: {}`により、`notify`ジョブではGITHUB_TOKENが一切の権限を持たなくなります。

このジョブはDiscord webhookへのHTTP POSTリクエストのみを行うため、GitHub APIへのアクセスは不要です。明示的に権限を制限することで、以下のメリットがあります：

- ✅ **最小権限の原則**: 必要最小限の権限のみを付与
- ✅ **攻撃面の縮小**: トークンが漏洩しても影響を最小化
- ✅ **セキュリティベストプラクティス**: GitHub Advanced Securityの推奨に準拠

## 影響範囲

- ✅ 既存の機能に影響なし（notifyジョブはGITHUB_TOKENを使用していない）
- ✅ CI/CDの動作は変更なし
- ✅ セキュリティのみ向上

## 参考

- [GitHub Actions: Permissions for GITHUB_TOKEN](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/automatic-token-authentication#permissions-for-the-github_token)
- [Security hardening for GitHub Actions](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-permissions)

## 関連

Closes #43 (github-advanced-securityの警告)

## Summary

Refactor `handle_action` (~1160 lines) into a pure reducer and an EffectRunner to improve testability and separation of concerns.

**Key changes:**
- `reducer.rs`: Pure state transitions only (no I/O, no `Instant::now()`)
- `effect_runner.rs`: Executes side effects (DB fetch, render, console spawn)
- `Effect` enum: Declarative representation of all side effects
- Time is passed as parameter to reducer for deterministic testing

## Architecture

```
Event → reduce(state, action, now) → Vec<Effect>

```

body:
The new function `normalize_by_observation` is intended to be used as a decorator for the CRPS functions in this package. It requires the observations to either be the 2nd positional argument or given as a keyword argument.

I tested for typical errors in argument handling as well as for the consistency of the CRPS results which must be in [0, 1] after normalization.

Note:
- The resulting value is not guaranteed to be <= 1, because the (original) CRPS value can be larger than the normalization factor computed from the observations `y`.
- If the observations are all close to zero, then the normalization is done by 1, so the CRPS can be > 1 in this case, too.

body:
pytest-asyncio runs fixture setup and teardown in different async tasks,
which causes anyio's cancel scope to fail with "Attempted to exit cancel
scope in a different task than it was entered in" when using MCP's
stdio_client (which uses anyio task groups internally).

pytest-anyio (bundled with anyio) runs setup and teardown in the same
task, fixing this incompatibility.

Changes:
- Replace pytest-asyncio with anyio==4.12.0 in test dependencies
- Remove asyncio_mode config from pyproject.toml
- Remove anyio_backend fixture from conftest.py
- Change @pytest.mark.asyncio to @pytest.mark.anyio in all tests

Task 5 requires implementing REST API endpoints for story creation and management with input validation and error handling.

## Status

All required endpoints are **already implemented** in the codebase from previous work (PR #33). No code changes needed.

## Implemented Endpoints

- **POST /api/stories/generate** - AI-powered story generation from summary
  - Zod validation (50-2000 chars summary, 1-20 chapters)
  - JWT authentication required
  - Strict rate limiting (5 req/15min)
  
- **GET /api/stories** - List stories with access control
  - Returns published stories for unauthenticated users
  - Returns published + own stories for authenticated users
  
- **GET /api/stories/:id** - Retrieve specific story
  - Access control: published stories or author's own unpublished stories
  
- **PUT /api/stories/:id** - Update story metadata
  - Validates title, summary, published status
  - Author-only authorization
  
- **DELETE /api/stories/:id** - Remove story
  - Author-only authorization

```typescript
  summary: z.string()
    .min(50, 'Summary must be at least 50 characters')
    .max(2000, 'Summary must not exceed 2000 characters'),
  numberOfChapters: z.number().int().min(1).max(20).default(5)
});

  try {
    const validatedData = generateStorySchema.parse(req.body);
    // ... AI generation logic
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof ZodError) {
      res.status(400).json({ error: 'Validation failed', details: error.errors });
    }
    // ... other error cases
  }
};
```

Routes configured with layered middleware (rate limiting → authentication → controller).

body:
### Motivation
- Keypresses on desktop could trigger global handlers and cause crashes or unintended behavior when focus was inside other inputs or before the grid was hydrated. 
- The previous implementation attached a global `window` keydown listener that lacked guards for editable targets and focus management. 
- The goal is to scope keyboard handling to the crossword area on desktop and prevent stray key events from mutating grid state.

### Description
- Added `gridWrapperRef` and moved keyboard handling to the crossword container with an `onKeyDown` handler to scope events to the grid. 
- Introduced `isEditableTarget` guard to ignore events when the `target` or `document.activeElement` is an input, textarea, select, or contenteditable element. 
- Focus management: the container is `tabIndex={0}` and is focused when a cell is activated on desktop (no change to mobile behavior). 
- Adjusted `handleKeyDown` signature and early-return logic so typing only affects the puzzle when appropriate and to avoid global `window` listeners.

### Testing
- Ran the regression test file with Vitest using `npm test -- --run tests/regression/crossword-keypress.test.tsx`. 
- Test results: the file passed with 2/2 tests succeeding (no crashes, and no parent sync loop). 
- Test run used the project test harness (`vitest`) and completed successfully. 
- No automated tests failed after the changes.

### Motivation
- Provide a way to request GPX output that includes elevation data without changing existing API callers. 
- Make it easy to request elevation-enriched GPX from the client and helper layers. 

### Description
- Added an overload `suspend fun getRouteGpx(profile: Profile, routeRequest: RouteRequest, includeElevation: Boolean): String` to `OrsClient`. 
- Implemented the overload in `DefaultOrsClient` to set `routeRequest.elevation = true` when `includeElevation` is `true` and call the existing `api.getRouteGpx` endpoint. 
- Added convenience extension overloads in `RouteHelper` (`getRouteGpx` for start/end and for coordinate lists) that accept `includeElevation` and delegate to the new `OrsClient` overload. 

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed as part of this change. 
- Changes were limited to API surface and helper overloads and preserve existing `getRouteGpx` behavior for callers that do not opt into elevation.
